A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Auto-GDA study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E are readable and can be matched despite extensive reflow and added appendix experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding-verification experiments, including benchmark performance, ablations, inference timings, and additional analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on initial-label corruption, synthetic-data quantity, selection-objective terms, and generation time.

M1.justification: The generation, augmentation, certainty-update, sample-selection, and fine-tuning procedure remains unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. The three objective terms, augmentation strategies, model architectures, and Appendix E prompts are retained. New single-term variants are experimental ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RAGTruth summarization and QA, LFQA-Verification, and SummEdits, with the same auxiliary source corpora. New experiments vary synthetic-training labels and quantities within this coverage; they introduce no new evaluation task or population.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain the same NLI models, LLMs, classical UDA methods, pseudo-labeling methods, and few-shot-data baseline. The source-data comparison in v1 Table 13 survives as v2 Table 15. The new data-size experiment reuses the existing few-shot baseline.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes RAGTruth samples per evidence from 12 to 8, while retaining dataset totals and main scores; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Additional protocols introduce 50% initial-label corruption, 0.5x-8x few-shot-data sizes, single-term objective controls, and generation-stage timing. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, and core fine-tuning settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix D.4 tests corrupted initial hard labels, D.6 tests whether generating more few-shot data substitutes for Auto-GDA, D.7 isolates individual selection terms, and D.10 profiles computational stages. These supplement the existing teacher-score noise, augmentation, dataset-size, and UDA analyses rather than merely redisplaying them.

E5.justification: v2 specifies five runs with different initial-generation seeds for the new corruption experiment and identifies the RAGTruth objective ablations as single-run results in Table 14. Repeated-run averages and uncertainty reporting already existed in v1. No increased repetition of retained experiments or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1-3 retain their numerical results, but substantial supplementary findings are added. The corruption study reports LFQA ROC-AUC of 0.914 ± 0.007 versus 0.925 ± 0.009 without corruption. Table 13 reports few-shot-baseline averages declining from 0.860 at 0.5x data to 0.841 at 8x. Tables 14 and 16 add objective-term results and generation timings.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical definitions, Propositions 1-2, and Appendix B derivations and proofs are retained. Section 4.4 changes the prose description from adding to subtracting expected utility, matching the subtraction already present in v1 Equation 3.

C1.justification: The abstract drops 'often' from its teacher-outperformance claim, making that statement less qualified. The introduction still says 'often,' and Section 5.1 retains the three-out-of-four qualification. The central contributions and claims of near-supervised performance and approximately tenfold lower inference latency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes robustness to filtering and explains synthetic-data saturation through repetitive generation and possible overfitting. Section 6 removes the explanation that UDA fails because embedding methods miss semantics, adds guidance favoring pretrained verifiers when adaptation is too costly, and identifies end-to-end RAG evaluation as future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, explicitly identifies validation ROC-AUC as the Optuna selection objective, and recommends coefficient settings for limited tuning budgets. It also documents generation-stage timings and profiling hardware. Most implementation details, checkpoints, preprocessing instructions, and prompts were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ru et al. on RAGChecker and Wang et al. on noise-robust fine-tuning, and removes Santhanam et al. from the hallucination motivation. The RAGTruth author/year revision and MiniCheck publication update refer to existing works. Classical UDA discussion is condensed and moved to Appendix A without changing the principal positioning.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence largely survive. v2 condenses related work, moves its detailed UDA discussion to Appendix A, clarifies method and tuning explanations, edits the conclusion, and adds appendix subsections. These are localized revisions rather than extensive rewriting of the existing paper.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference-wide formatting with narrower text, new heading and header styles, and extensive reflow of figures, tables, and captions. Figure 5 is redrawn with labeled axes. An unnumbered corruption-results table and Tables 13, 14, and 16 are added; existing displays are retained, including v1 Table 13 as v2 Table 15.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional support for robustness and the selection criterion, tests the alternative of simply generating more data, and makes adaptation costs and reproduction instructions clearer. The gains are limited by single-run RAGTruth objective ablations and a runtime-table inconsistency: Table 16 labels its large dataset as summarization while the accompanying text and sample counts indicate QA. Overall, the additions improve confidence and usability without fundamentally changing the evidence supporting the paper's main conclusions.
